The agenda covers public communication, an Operations Research course update, a Secondary Summer Success students update, a district/superintendent goals discussion, board committee assignments, other business, and adjournment. **Meeting**
Workshop meeting of the Board of Trustees, Troy School District, September 17, 2013, 6:00 PM, Administration Building, 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098. Agenda: public communication; Operations Research course update; Secondary Summer Success students update; district/superintendent goals discussion; board committee assignments; other; adjournment.

**Operations Research course update**
Presented by Kris Karbon and Carol Machak. Goals of Project Mindset: improve math students' abilities to formulate and solve multi-step problems and interpret results, and improve students' attitudes toward mathematics. Precalculus teachers piloted a Project Mindset unit with professional development from Wayne State instructors; Athens teachers then sought the full course as a fourth-year elective. Athens High School had 2 sections in 2012-13 and has 4 sections in 2013-14.

OPERATIONS RESEARCH COURSE UPDATE. The Board of Education study session presentation for September 17, 2013 is credited to Kris Karbon and Carol Machak. It frames three questions: what are the goals of the Operations Research class; how does Operations Research fit into the Troy School District's mathematics curriculum; and what kind of problems are students working on in the course. A Common Core Pathway slide is included. Under "History of Operations Research in Troy," the presentation states that Precalculus teachers were asked to pilot a Project Mindset unit and received professional development from Wayne State instructors, and that teachers from Athens expressed interest in offering the full course as a fourth-year elective. In 2012-13 Athens High School had 2 sections of Operations Research; in 2013-14 Athens High School has 4 sections.

STUDENT PROJECT EXAMPLE. The illustrative student problem is titled "Which Sport Should Lauren Mitchell Play?" SECONDARY SUMMER SUCCESS STUDENTS UPDATE. The Summer Success Academy data presentation for the Board Workshop of September 17, 2013 lists three program goals: reducing the summer slide; increasing student confidence (attitudes about school); and increased student retention (graduation rates of at-risk students). Cohort groups are a pilot program in Summer 2011 (juniors); the 1st Summer Success Group in Summer 2012 (sophomores), following which the district restructured the identification process to target students who can most benefit from the program; and the 2nd Summer Success Group in Summer 2013 (freshmen). Under increasing student confidence and attitudes about school, the middle school staffs identified 95 at-risk students who could benefit from the program, 48 students voluntarily attended (51%), and 94% successfully completed and received math and English credit.

Under increased retention and graduation rates of at-risk students, results are shown for the 1st Summer Success Group, Summer 2012 (sophomores), comparing 48 students that attended with 47 students who did not attend. Of the 48 who attended, 26 students are on track to graduate (55%), 22 students received 1 E or more (45%), and there were 22 E's in math or English. Of the 47 who did not attend, 24 students are on track to graduate (49%), 23 students received 1 E or more (51%), and there were 19 E's in math or English. Next steps and on-going work include continuing to monitor the identification process for at-risk students who benefit from the Summer Success Program, building a mentoring program at the high school to continue to support Summer Success students, implementation of an elementary Grade 3 to 4 summer program, and implementation of a Middle School SSA program.

BOARD COMMITTEE ASSIGNMENTS. CAPE (Citizens and Parents for Education), 4773 Foxcroft Drive, Troy, MI 48085-3530, reported through steering committee chair Dave Lambert. The ballot proposition asks whether the Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan shall borrow not to exceed One Hundred Twenty Five Million ($125,000,000) Dollars in general obligation unlimited tax bonds for remodeling and re-equipping buildings, technology, additions, sites and buses. Bonds may be outstanding not more than fifteen (15) years exclusive of refunding; the estimated millage in the first year is 1.84 mills ($1.84 per $1,000 of taxable value) and the estimated simple average annual millage over fifteen years is 2.93 mills ($2.93 per $1,000 of taxable value). Under the School Bond Qualification and Loan Program the district has $93,605,000 of qualified bonds outstanding and $0 of qualified loans. Proceeds must be audited and cannot pay salaries or operating expenses. Campaign material shows 4.7 mills currently and 4.7 mills if the bond passes and urges a YES vote November 5th; testimonials come from Bruce Bloomingdale, Robert Preston and Jo Rhoads, and a CAPE letter from Daniel Fair cites 35 years in Troy, five children in Troy Schools, six grandchildren and a newest elementary school 30 years old.

SUPERINTENDENT'S ANNUAL REPORT AND GOALS (Dr. Fowler). The 2012/2013 goals were college and career readiness; interventions for lowest performing subgroups; preparation for the November 2013 bond election; and a data processing review. Targets included 100% of 4th grade teachers observing other classrooms four times in 2012-2013 and 100% of 5th grade teachers in 2013-2014, 24 teachers trained in MI CLASS literacy practices in grades 6-12, claim-evidence-reasoning writing samples in grades 6-11, and a math support class adding 3 hours of instruction per week for middle school students. Bond preparation included a facility assessment study by TMP Architecture covering site, roofing, plumbing/HVAC and electrical, a Technology Advisory Committee assessment, a 9-year bus replacement schedule, a community survey completed Thursday, January 10, 2013, Board review at the January 22nd workshop and presentation of the bond amount at the February 5th Board Meeting. The data processing review put the current Finance/Human Resources system at a cost per student of $12+; after a Summer 2012 demonstration TSD chose Oakland Schools' Tyler Munis alongside 22 other Oakland County districts over the next 4 fiscal years, subsidized for the first five years and approximately $10 per student thereafter, with a transition date set by June 30, 2013 and commitment letters due late Fall 2013. Under the new accountability system, schools and districts must have 85% of all students and student groups proficient by 2021-2022, a student group being any group of 30 or more students, with Annual Measureable Objectives calculated from the 2011-2012 proficiency rate.
